provenance: 160 synthetic cases authored and labeled by gpt-6-luna; independently audited by another gpt-6-luna; 26 cases reviewed by the parent agent after threshold freeze and before predictions. Four ambiguous ownership labels corrected before predictions. No human ground truth.
limitations: Short authored exchanges; some assistant replies explicitly state the interpretation, making these easier than natural conversations.
The eight additional instruction families were withheld from prompt and threshold development.
The dataset becomes inspected development material after this evaluation; do not tune on it and call it fresh again.

instructions.title: Track issues
instructions.text: Catch issues mentioned in my sessions and keep their status current.
examples: The upload spinner stays active after the server returns an error.
The duplicate invoice issue is fixed in release 2.8 and verified against BILL-19.

instructions.title: Track deferred work
instructions.text: Keep track of work we decide to leave for later, and update it when we finish it.
examples: We agreed to postpone the webhook retry interface until after the billing cutover.
The review we parked for next cycle is complete under UI-91.

instructions.title: Keep architectural decisions
instructions.text: Keep our architectural decisions and why we made them.
examples: We chose append-only events so audit history survives account merges.
We kept server rendering because the initial view must work before JavaScript loads.

instructions.title: Track external API constraints
instructions.text: Track external API constraints and the workarounds we use, including changes to previously recorded constraints.
examples: The mail provider expires upload links after ten minutes, so we refresh them before retrying.
The shipping API raised its burst allowance, so we can relax the old client throttle.

instructions.title: Track dated customer commitments
instructions.text: Keep track of firm, dated commitments we make to customers and update them when they change or are fulfilled.
examples: I promised Northstar a signed usage export by March 18, before its finance review.
We delivered Lumen's SAML mapping on the revised date agreed in the account thread.

instructions.title: Track dependency license constraints
instructions.text: Keep track of license restrictions on third-party dependencies, the choices we make to comply, and later changes to those constraints.
examples: The chart package is AGPL, which conflicts with distribution, so we replaced it with the MIT edition.
Counsel approved the SDK's MPL terms after confirming the file-level obligations.

instructions.title: Track localization mistakes
instructions.text: Keep track of locale-specific text and formatting mistakes we find and update their status when corrected or ruled out.
examples: The Italian checkout plural is wrong above one item; LOC-53 is open.
The Thai currency spacing issue was fixed in build 7.12 and verified by the language team.

instructions.title: Track unanswered product questions
instructions.text: Keep track of product questions that still need a named person's answer, and update them when answered or cancelled.
examples: Mina still needs to confirm whether an owner can revoke an invitation after acceptance.
The report visibility question was closed in PDP-204 after Theo supplied the policy answer.

instructions.title: Track evidence against hypotheses
instructions.text: Keep track of concrete findings that contradict an explicit hypothesis and update the status if later evidence changes the conclusion.
examples: We thought retries caused the delay, but the trace shows the first request waits on DNS.
A free account reproduced the problem, challenging our claim that it only affects large tenants.

instructions.title: Track operational monitoring gaps
instructions.text: Keep track of missing operational metrics, alerts, or health checks that leave a service failure hard to detect, and update their status when covered.
examples: The reconciliation job can stop silently because nobody alerts on its last-success time.
The worker lag alert now covers the delayed queue that previously had no threshold.

instructions.title: Track approval requirements for destructive actions
instructions.text: Keep track of accepted requirements for explicit approval before destructive or irreversible actions, including later changes to those requirements.
examples: The retention rule requires a second administrator to approve a permanent tenant purge.
Security approved re-authentication by the key owner before production credentials are revoked.

instructions.title: Track recurring workflow preferences
instructions.text: Keep track of my recurring preferences for how we work, and update them when I change them.
examples: Please include the command behind a result in future investigation summaries too.
Going forward, show the smallest useful diff first when you review changes with me.
